title: The Darkest Things Found in the Everglades
igCaption:
Two airliners, a python that tried to swallow an alligator, and a 215-pound snake full of eggs. What's been found out in the Everglades.

Would you go out there at night?

Sources: Wikipedia: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401, Wikipedia: ValuJet Flight 592, Conservancy of Southwest Florida, Associated Press

#everglades #florida #miami #southflorida

scenes.text: People have found some seriously disturbing things deep inside the Everglades.

location.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crash site

scenes.text: December twenty-ninth, nineteen seventy-two, just before midnight. Eastern Air Lines Flight four oh one was on approach to Miami when the crew got fixated on a landing gear light. The autopilot slipped out of altitude hold, and the jet slowly descended into the sawgrass. One hundred one people died. Seventy-five survived.
scenes.caption: December 29, 1972, just before midnight. Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 was on approach to Miami when the crew got fixated on a landing gear light. The autopilot slipped out of altitude hold, and the jet slowly descended into the sawgrass. 101 people died. 75 survived.

location.name: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crash site

scenes.text: A few miles away, on May eleventh, nineteen ninety-six, ValuJet Flight five ninety-two went down about ten minutes after leaving Miami. Mislabeled oxygen generators caught fire in the cargo hold. All one hundred ten people on board were killed. It's still the deadliest air crash in Florida history.
scenes.caption: A few miles away, on May 11, 1996, ValuJet Flight 592 went down about 10 minutes after leaving Miami. Mislabeled oxygen generators caught fire in the cargo hold. All 110 people on board were killed. It's still the deadliest air crash in Florida history.

scenes.text: Then there are the pythons. In two thousand five, researchers in Everglades National Park found a thirteen-foot Burmese python that had tried to swallow a six-foot alligator. Both animals were dead, the alligator still partly inside the snake.
scenes.caption: Then there are the pythons. In 2005, researchers in Everglades National Park found a 13-foot Burmese python that had tried to swallow a 6-foot alligator. Both animals were dead, the alligator still partly inside the snake.

scenes.text: And the record breaker. Researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida caught a female python nearly eighteen feet long weighing two hundred fifteen pounds. Inside her were one hundred twenty-two developing eggs, and deer hooves in her stomach. Pythons have been breeding out here since at least two thousand.
scenes.caption: And the record breaker. Researchers from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida caught a female python nearly 18 feet long weighing 215 pounds. Inside her were 122 developing eggs, and deer hooves in her stomach. Pythons have been breeding out here since at least 2000.
scenes.sub: A Florida record at the time
